title: Stateful deletion manifests and replayable erasure workflow for analytics
creator: Nadia Chen
description:
Background: Console telemetry and usage analytics live across multiple storage layers (raw S3 event buckets, clickhouse summary tables, and downstream Snowflake datasets). Current ad-hoc deletion paths are brittle: scrubbing jobs run per-store, lack a canonical source of truth, and are difficult to audit for compliance. Goal: implement a stateful, auditable deletion manifest system and a replayable erasure workflow that orchestrates scrubbing and eventual purge across all analytics sinks with verifiable proofs of completion.

Scope: (1) Manifest schema and authoritative manifest store; (2) Orchestrator service that consumes manifests and emits idempotent per-sink deletion commands; (3) Soft-delete / tombstone lifecycle with purge scheduling and KMS-signed manifests for audit; (4) Queryable audit trail and reconcile job to detect drift between manifests and sink state.

Out of scope for this ticket: UI for triggering manifests (will be a follow-up PM ticket), storage-level hardware erasure for on-prem racks.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical manifest schema v1 defined and checked into repo (JSON Schema + example) and stored in S3 path s3://redwood-analytics/manifests/erasure-manifest-v1/

Authoritative manifest index implemented in console-postgres table analytics_deletion_manifests with columns (manifest_id, scope, created_by, manifest_s3_path, status, signed_by_kms_key, tombstone_at, purge_at)

Orchestrator service consumes manifests from git/s3/index and emits idempotent deletion commands to three sink adapters: raw-s3 (object delete or overwrite), clickhouse (DELETE/TTL marker), snowflake (metadata flag + scheduled purge), with at-least-once delivery semantics
Every executed manifest gets a completion record containing per-sink checksums/tombstone counts and a KMS-signed completion token written back to the manifest index
Reconcile job compares manifest expectations to sink state and raises an alert if >0.5% of rows expected to be deleted are still visible after grace period
E2E test coverage with a local minio + test ClickHouse container demonstrating a manifest lifecycle: created -> consumed -> tombstoned -> purged.
tasks: Design and finalize erasure-manifest-v1 JSON Schema (fields: manifest_id, scope, selectors, reason, created_by, created_at, tombstone_at, purge_at, sinks, checksum, kms_signature)
Add analytics_deletion_manifests table DDL and migration script
Implement manifest writer utility (CLI) to upload manifests to S3 and register in index (with KMS sign step)
Build orchestrator microservice with a consumer loop: poll index -> claim manifest -> emit per-sink commands -> write per-sink status -> finalize manifest
Implement sink adapters: s3-adapter, clickhouse-adapter, snowflake-adapter. Adapters must be idempotent and support dry-run mode
Add reconcile worker that runs nightly and posts findings to #console-privacy Slack channel and Console Ops dashboard
Add logging and tracing hooks (trace/span for manifest_id) and ensure logs include manifest_id and per-sink command IDs
Create unit + integration tests and CI job that runs the minio+clickhouse+snowflake emulator test matrix
Prepare PR with migration, schema, and orchestrator; request security review and compliance signoff
technical_notes: Manifest store: immutable JSON blobs in S3 + authoritative index in Postgres to enable SQL queries and ACID claim semantics
Signing: each manifest must be signed using KMS asymmetric key and signature stored alongside manifest. Completion records also signed to prevent tampering.
Idempotency: adapters must accept manifest_id and idempotency_token; deletions recorded in sink-level tombstone tables to make replays safe
Retention windows: default tombstone grace = 30 days, purge window = 180 days. These are configurable per-manifest scope.

Throughput concerns: large manifests may target billions of events. Orchestrator must support chunked command streams and backpressure to adapters. Use chunk size heuristics and rate-limited parallelism

Failure modes: if adapter fails mid-manifest, orchestrator should mark manifest as "incomplete" and allow retriable claim after backoff. Finalizer should require all sink statuses = SUCCESS before signing completion
Auditability: reconcile job computes a deterministic checksum of leftover keys for S3 and a row-count diff for ClickHouse/Snowflake; attach results to manifest completion record
Privacy-preserving logs: adapters must never log raw PII. All logs must reference hashed selectors (sha256 with a rotation salt stored in KMS) to enable debugging without exposing data
risks: Large-scale purges can accidentally create high load on ClickHouse and Snowflake leading to query contention — need throttling and canary runs
Edge cases where derived artifacts (materialized aggregates, ML feature stores) still contain PII even after source deletion — requires inventory and downstream connectors
Regulatory requirement for provable deletion may require additional cryptographic proofs beyond current KMS-signed manifests
Human error in manifest creation could be destructive; CLI should default to dry-run and require 2-step confirmation for global scopes
